answer: Each seat is bound to one registered legal entity, and the public company register supplies the check: a seat may claim only an entity whose filing is active and not already tied to another seat, so one certificate bears one pigment and a duplicate claim is refused at intake. A farm wanting a thousand seats must keep a thousand filings alive, each with its own registered agent, address and annual report, and the yearly delta between declared and observed activity is what a raven audit reads; an entity found dormant loses its seat and its filing history stays public.
